candidates.summary: gatewayHost accepts IPv4 shorthands (127.1, 0x7f000001, 2130706433) as DNS names, though browsers rewrite them to dotted-quad
candidates.failure_scenario: `-ipfs-gateway https://127.1` (or https://0x7f000001) passes normalizeIPFSGateway, and the CSP gets `https://127.1`. A WHATWG browser parses the rewritten src as https://127.0.0.1/..., so the host-source can never match: every IPFS image is blocked while startup reports the gateway valid. The same spelling slips past the onHost check against a canonical host of 127.0.0.1
candidates.verify_by: read the regex: every label of `127.1` and `0x7f000001` matches [a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?; then load a page whose CSP img-src is https://127.1 with in a headful browser and watch the violation
candidates.evidence: ipfs.go:21 regex has no rule against an all-numeric or 0x last label; isLoopbackHost only gates http, so https values of this shape are accepted
